title: TianheEngine: Hierarchy-aware Adaptive Partitioning System for Trillion-scale Graph Processing
problem: Traditional graph partitioning strategies neglect hierarchical communication variances in modern HPC systems, causing prohibitive cross-layer communication overhead when processing trillion-scale graphs across thousands of nodes.
motivation: Multi-trillion-edge graphs require partitioning strategies that exploit the communication hierarchy of underlying HPC architectures to minimize inter-node communication costs.
method: TianheEngine: hierarchy-aware adaptive partitioning system that exploits communication hierarchy and graph sparsity characteristics to improve communication efficiency in distributed graph processing.
key_novelty: First partitioning system to systematically exploit hierarchical communication costs in HPC systems for trillion-scale graph processing, validated across 79,024 computing nodes.
contributions: Adaptive partitioning based on communication topology and graph structure
Outperforms state-of-the-art graph partitioning and parallel graph systems
Superior performance to top-ranked Graph500 systems
limitations: Evaluation on proprietary supercomputer (Tianhe) limits reproducibility; specific hierarchical characteristics of Tianhe may not generalize to other architectures.
